results.quote: Given a set X of n integers in [t], we can compute \Sigma(X)\cap[t] in \widetilde{O}(t) deterministic time.
Given a set X of n integers in [t], we can compute \Sigma(X)\cap[t] in \widetilde{O}(|\Sigma(X)\cap[t]|\sqrt{n}) deterministic time.
Given a set X of n integers in [t], we can compute \Sigma(X)\cap[t] in \widetilde{O}(|\Sigma(X)\cap[t]|^{4/3}) deterministic time.

results.previous_best: randomized \widetilde{O}(t^{2-\varepsilon'}) via reduction to min-plus convolution (Cygan et al.)
results.quote: In particular, this implies a deterministic O(t^2/2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log t})})-time algorithm for 0-1 knapsack, by using Chan and Williams' deterministic min-plus matrix multiplication algorithm [CW21] together with a known reduction from min-plus matrix multiplication to convolution [BCD+14].

results.previous_best: randomized reduction from all-targets 0-1 knapsack to min-plus convolution (Cygan et al.)
results.quote: If min-plus convolution for two real vectors of length n could be computed in T(n) deterministic time, then the all-capacities version of the 0-1 knapsack problem could be solved in \widetilde{O}(T(t)) deterministic time.
